name: Augsburg Diesel engine
description: Rudolf Diesel and industrial collaborators developed a working compression-ignition engine in the 1890s.

impact.note: Its descendants drive ships, lorries, trains and farm machines in many societies; heavy transport was reorganised around it, and a long engine line followed.

places.note: Present-day country or region reference; ancient political boundaries are not implied.

date.basis: The cited source dates the episode.

events.statement: Rudolf Diesel and collaborators produced a functioning diesel engine after a series of experiments.
events.caveats: The source dates a functional engine to the year; the exact acceptance date, operating conditions and first customer are not established here.

evidence.supports: The Deutsches Museum dates the functional result and identifies Augsburg and Krupp as collaborators.

contributions.resource: Developed the engine with industrial collaborators

evidence.supports: The museum identifies Diesel and the collaborating companies.

contributions.resource: Collaborated in engine development at Augsburg

evidence.supports: MAN describes Diesel and factory technicians working together in 1897.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest episode established by the cited evidence for this precisely scoped record; not a claim of global origin.

caveats: The 1897 result was preceded by years of experimental work, and later vehicles and engines are not identified with this prototype.

research.note: Initial evidence-backed admission; classifications and historical interpretations await independent review. Independent review checked cited event dates, wording and, where marked, numerical measures; other facets retain their original status.
